newsitem.title: EGYPT: Iran's Velayati in Cairo on landmark visit.
newsitem.headline: Iran's Velayati in Cairo on landmark visit.

text.p: Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati arrived in Cairo on Monday for the first high-level meeting between Egypt and Iran since Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak accused Tehran of trying to kill him in 1995.
Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa met Velayati at Cairo airport and the two men left to hold formal talks.
Velayati said he was in Cairo to give President Hosni Mubarak a handwritten invitation from Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani to an Islamic summit in Tehran in December.
The Iranian official is due to meet Mubarak on Tuesday.
"Egypt is an influential state in the Islamic world. It can play an important role in solving the problems that face the Islamic world," Velayati told reporters at the airport.

"My visit to Egypt will be a chance to exchange views on a number of Islamic problems and there is no doubt that when contacts increase between the two countries it will help create a better atmosphere," he added.
Iran severed its diplomatic relations with Egypt in 1979 following its signing of a peace treaty with Israel.

Egypt has accused Iran and Sudan of continuing support for the al-Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group), the largest organisation fighting to set up a strict Islamic state in Egypt. Both Sudan and Iran deny this.

Asked to comment on charges that Iran was supporting militants in Egypt, Velayati said: "This is not true. Iran does not support any terrorist groups. It does not and will not aid such organisations".
Iran was also accused of being behind the attempted assassination of Mubarak during the Egyptian leader's visit to Ethiopia in 1995.
Velayati last visited Cairo in 1994 to attend a Non-Aligned Movement meeting of foreign ministers.
